costBasis: Per-instance cost averaged within each scenario, then across the four scenarios; not actual billing. Subscription-plan runs (Claude, GPT, Gemini) are priced as their share of the Claude $100 plan's weekly quota times that plan's weekly price (taskPoints); DeepSeek V4.1 Flash and GLM 5.3 (run through OpenCode Go, a plan with no efficiency ratio E) have no cost, and Strata is at its local running cost

instanceCost.anthropic: Per-request tokens from the saved session (agent.json measurementFacts) at the anthropic rates below (cache writes at the 1-hour rate; Haiku by prompt length), API-equivalent USD, times the Claude plan's E (1 by definition); then the plan-fee conversion
instanceCost.openai: Token counts at the openai rates below (API-equivalent USD) times the Codex plan's E, then the plan-fee conversion
instanceCost.google: Token counts at the google rates below (output includes thinking) times Gemini's estimated E, then the plan-fee conversion
instanceCost.opencode: No cost is computed: the runs used an OpenCode Go plan whose per-token prices are not published and no E is applied (statspec 2.7: a plan category without E does not enter the shared cost axis). The supplement still holds per-request list-price USD for these runs for reference; the page does not use it. The list prices below document that figure only
instanceCost.strata: Local running cost from the instance work seconds and the localRunningCost settings below

gpt-6.2-sol.longContext: input above 272K: input and cache x2, output x1.5 (not applied: records hold totals only)

strata-iq3_xxs.notes: Home PC with an RTX 3080 Ti 12 GB, i9-13900 and 64 GB RAM. 400 W is a rough whole-system load estimate (350 W GPU board limit; memory-bound decoding usually draws less). Electricity is the Q1 2026 world household average (country-weighted). Maintenance covers wear parts at about USD 50 a year over about 2,500 loaded hours.

taskPoints.pointUsdSource: TASK_POINT_USD in ~/.claude/lib/conversion.py: one equivalent task point is worth $100 of Claude API (1/20 of a Max 20x weekly quota)

plan.name: Claude $100 plan
plan.weeklyPointsBasis: One week of the Claude $100 plan is about $536 of Claude API-priced use (= 5.36 points at pointUsd 100, E = 1 for Claude). Measured on the local Claude Max 20x plan on 2026-11-18 (usage.sh --calibrate: 0.0466 percentage points of weekly quota per API-priced USD at 11% used, so a full 20x week is about $2,146); the $100 plan is taken as 1/4 of the 20x quota. About +/-10% (a 1% rounding step at 11% used is about +/-9%; Claude Code's run cost uses its own price list). The status page's nominal convention (point = 1/20 of a 20x week) would give 5.0 points, 7% lower, inside that error. Carried over unchanged from the v2.4 factor so that Claude runs keep their v2.4 costs.

taskPoints.formula: cost USD = (equivalent task points of the run / plan.weeklyPoints) x weekly price of the plan, where weekly price = plan.monthlyUsd / plan.daysPerMonth x 7; equivalent task points = API-equivalent USD of the run x E of the plan category / pointUsd. Every plan run is multiplied by the same constant relative to API-equivalent USD x E, so ratios between plan runs equal the ratios of their task points.
taskPoints.efficiencyMeaning: E = Claude's historical cost of the same kind of finished work / this plan category's cost of it (taskpts.py); the category aggregate is used for every model of the plan, not each model's own E

anthropic.source: taskpts.json scope claude (model null) on 2026-11-26; 1 by definition (coverage 91%, 28-day window)

openai.source: taskpts.json scope codex (model null) on 2026-11-26 (28-day window, 1659 covered finished items); used for Sol, Terra and Luna alike

google.source: taskpts.json scope antigravity-gemini (model null) on 2026-11-26 (28-day window, 80 covered finished items, all Hydrogen; equals Hydrogen's own E, whose coverage is 100%). The category's coverage is below the status page's 30% display threshold, so it is an estimate; it is applied to Neon too, whose own E is not measured. The Antigravity pipeline was removed on 2026-11-17, so it will not be updated.

taskPoints.snapshotNote: Refreshed once at publication (v2-publish, statspec D5) from the status page's taskpts.json (taken 2026-11-26, 28-day window ending that day); v1 keeps its own 2026-11-18 snapshot. plan.weeklyPoints keeps the 2026-11-18 calibration (taskpts.json holds no new calibration). The status page's opencode category (E about 5.6, scope-level, not per model) is not applied: DeepSeek and GLM have no cost on this page.
